## Introduction

This is a simple demo to carry out variable selection 

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(fspls2)

devtools::load_all( "~/github/fspls2/R")
  transform_x=getTransform(pow = 1,    ## transformations raise to the powers indicated here.  Default is 1 but can add others
                            n_random=1,perm=FALSE ## number of random transformations, also used in stopping critera
                            )
  


```

```{r example}
  examples = c("binomial", "gaussian", "ordinal", "multinomial");
#example="gaussian"
  



  #FUNCTION TO SHOW HOW TO RUN EACH EXAMPLE
  runExample<-function(example,nfold=5){
   flags = getFlags(nfold = nfold);
    fi = system.file("extdata", paste0(example,"_data.rds"), package = "fspls2")
    if (fi == "") stop("Could not find extdata/", example, "_data.rds in fspls2 package")
    dataset = readRDS(fi)
       ## set up the objects
    folds = getFolds(nrow(dataset$y), nfold = nfold)
    dh = dataH$new(dataset$dataset, y = dataset$y,    nme=example, flags=flags, folds = folds)##, family="gaussian")
    ##Step 1. run variable selection 
    datasH = list(dh)
    analysis =analysisEnv$new(flags=flags, dbDir=NULL)
    data_types = dh$data_types();
    phens = dh$pheno()$all
    variables=analysis$select(datasH, phens, transform_x)
    allvar_table = analysis$tabulate_variables(variables)

        #Step 2. make models with selected variables
    dh$update(phens = phens, flags = flags, transform_x = transform_x, data_types = data_types, folds = folds)

    all_models =dh$makeAllModels(variables);
    dh$tabulateBetas(all_models)
    
    ##OPTIONAL IF BEAM>1
    if(flags$beam>1){
        all_models = dh$updateEnsemble(all_models)
    }

    #dh$plot_angles()
    #optionally get predictions
    predictions = dh$extractPredictions(all_models, prob=TRUE)
    
    eval1= dh$evaluate(predictions)

    
    #optionally visualise the predictions
        pred_plots = dh$plotPredictions(predictions, merge_beam=FALSE, keep_cv=FALSE)

    #Step 3. evaluate the models
   
    
    ## Now visuaise the resultsy
    ggps1=analysis$plotEval(eval1,legend=T, grid_x=c("subpheno","pheno", "measure"), grid_y=c("cv_index"),linetype="combined",
                   color="beam",##"full_model"
                   shape=c("combined"),sep_by="data",
                   showranges=F,text="variable",
                   transformy=if(example=="gaussian") "log" else "probit",
                   scales="free",title =names(phens)[1], title1="pheno" ) #, grid="pheno~cv_full",showranges = F)
  evals_formatted= analysis$tabulateEvals(eval1)
    ##optionally get all predictions
    #predictions =     dh$extractPredictions(all_models)
    list(perf=ggps1, preds=pred_plots, formatted = evals_formatted)
  }


##iterative function carries out imputation of uncertain y values at the same time as feature selection
##only works for multinomial and binomial
runIterative<-function(example, prop_na=0.2, seed=42){
 
  flags$nfold=1 ## only works with one fold currently
  flags$min=1  ## need at least one variable
  flags$angles_only=FALSE ## works much better with pvalus
 # flags$angles_only = FALSE ## works better with angles_only=FALSE
     fi = system.file("extdata", paste0(example,"_data.rds"), package = "fspls2")
    dataset = readRDS(fi); 
    if(example=="binomial") dataset$y$y = factor(dataset$y$y, labels=c("A","B"))
    dataset$certainty = rep(1, nrow(dataset$y));
    set.seed(seed)
    na_inds1=sort(sample.int(nrow(dataset$y),nrow(dataset$y)*prop_na))
  dataset$certainty[na_inds1]=0.5;##1/length(levels(dataset$y[[1]]))
  #dataset$y[na_inds,] = NA
  
  flags$mult = 100
  flags$select_each_iteration = TRUE;
  results = fspls.iterative(dataset, flags, transform_x)
  #print(results$updates)
  print(data.frame(results$quantiles))
  na_remaining= length(which(results$certainty_new<0.90))
  message(paste("na remaining", na_remaining, "of", length(na_inds1)))  
  message(paste("error rate",results$error_rate))
 results_all =  list(input = data.frame(y = dataset$y, certainty=dataset$certainty ), output = data.frame(results$y_new, results$certainty_new), results = results)
 return(results_all)
}


```
Example 1
```{r, eval = FALSE}
ggp1=runExample("binomial", nfold=5);
ggp1
```

Iteratively replacing uncertain values
```{r, eval = FALSE}
## test Iterative works on binomial and multinomial
flags$angles_only = FALSE;

results = runIterative("binomial")
print(cbind(results$input, results$output))
```
